When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **3/10** (warning) vs VIX Spike tier **4/4** (extreme, **85%** probability)
The Crash Index scores damage already visible in prices. The VIX Spike scores what options buyers pay for protection ahead of time. Trust the VIX Spike for timing since options look forward, and let the Crash Index confirm when it climbs.
⚠ These two disagree: VIX backwardation active (tier **4**) vs **0** of **3** T1 confluences active (credit, small caps, yen)
Backwardation is the trigger leg of all three confluences, yet no confirming asset has joined it. Trust the confluences for sizing: the stress sits in index options and has not reached credit, small caps or yen.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian score **56** (accumulate) vs Divergence zone TOPPING with **27** bearish pairs against **3** bullish
Contrarian says fear is worth buying in part. Divergence says internal relationships are breaking. Trust divergence for size and accumulate only in small clips.
Today's tension
Options pay for an **85%** chance of a vol spike while price action stays orderly and leadership narrows.
Bull
The contrarian score sits at **56** (accumulate, partial signal), **0** of **3** confluences are active, and the Nasdaq 100 gained **+2.6%** over five days. Credit, small caps and yen flow have not joined the fear.
Bear
VIX Spike is at tier **4** of **4** with skew, backwardation and adaptive triggers all on. **69.8%** of **43** pairs are diverging, **27** bearish against **3** bullish, and the composite zone reads TOPPING.
The tell: Whether any of the three backwardation confluences (credit, small caps, yen) switches on. One firing means cash assets are confirming what options already price.
AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The market is split between a calm surface and a nervous options book. The Crash Index reads 3/10, the regime score is 66 (TRANSITION, mixed bias), and the macro regime is CONCENTRATION at only 55% confidence. Meanwhile VIX Spike sits at tier 4 of 4 with an 85% probability. Few stocks carry the index, and the options market is pricing that fragility.

For positioning, keep your core exposure and cut the size of new adds. The contrarian score of 56 supports buying weakness in small clips. The divergence picture, with 69.8% of pairs diverging and a net bias of 24 toward bearish, says you shouldn't buy it aggressively. Hold more cash than usual and favor the leaders that are still confirming, not the laggards that look cheap.

The main risk is that backwardation spreads from options into cash markets. Today 0 of 3 confluences are active, which is the main reason the stance stays cautious instead of defensive. If credit stress, small cap drawdown or yen safe haven flow switches on alongside backwardation, the read flips to reducing risk. If the Crash Index stays at 3 and tier 4 fades, the spike probability was a hedge bid and the regime resolves back toward a broader advance.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means two assets that normally move together are moving apart. Correlation drift is the change in how tightly they move together, comparing a recent window with a longer one.

The composite zone is TOPPING, with 69.8% of 43 pairs diverging, 27 bearish and 3 bullish. The mother jaws score is 100.

The sharpest drifts: QQQ against SPY went from +0.85 to -0.25, so the Nasdaq 100 no longer moves with the broad index. Regional banks against financials went from +0.22 to -0.68.

Visa against Mastercard went from +0.76 to -0.70, and AUD/JPY went from +0.38 to -0.17, a weaker risk appetite signal. Six pairs score 80, the DEEP DIVERG level.

When relationships this stable break together, the market is reshuffling leadership, and that tends to show up near tops. Watch whether QQQ and SPY re-couple.

If they do, the topping read loses weight.

Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Leadership is uneven in every region. In Asia the Nikkei leads at +2.9% while the Hang Seng lags at -3.2%.

In Europe the DAX holds at -0.7% and the CAC trails at -2.2%. In the US the Nasdaq 100 gained +2.6% and the Dow slipped -0.4%.

Crypto is firm, with Bitcoin at +2.7% and Ether at +1.1%. Money is rotating toward tech and Japan and away from Hong Kong and Europe.

For the US session, that favors growth leadership holding at the open, with the Dow and cyclicals as the weak side. Bitcoin leading Ether by 1.6 points says crypto buyers want the safest liquid exposure.

If the Nikkei gives back its gain, the US lead is exposed.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 3/10 · WARNING — 3+ signals, active surveillance
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

These two gauges measure different things, so a gap between them is coherent. The Crash Index at 3/10 counts damage that has already shown up in prices and breadth.

The VIX Spike Detector at tier 4/4 (85%) reads the options market, where skew, backwardation and the adaptive trigger are all active. Near term fear is priced above near term damage, which usually happens when buyers pay up for protection before the index breaks.

Trust the options read for timing and treat the 3/10 as the number that must rise before you cut exposure hard. With no confluence active, the stress has not spread to credit, small caps or the yen, so hedge rather than exit.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 3/10 — a few early signals are stirring; watch whether more line up.

How to read
Each row = an independent signal Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY. The structural (DXY, SKEW, MOVE) signal a regime change over 30-90 days. The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

How to read
Heat ranking: composite of RS (relative strength vs SPY), Momentum (price action 20-60d), Breadth (% stocks above SMA), Options flow, and Attention. Use top-5 as rotation focus.
Emerging industries: high velocity = screener scores accelerating this week vs prior baseline — potential early rotation signal.
Competitor themes: token frequency × recency across top finance Substacks — useful narrative context, not a trading signal.
Best R/R: only entries with an active screener leg (PULLBACK / BOTTOM / SMART_MONEY_SURGE etc.). EV% = probabilistic edge per trade. Cross-check with weekly chart before sizing.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
